# v1.2.16 — Every source back online

## Providers that were down are back (or gone)

A full sweep of every source found a handful that had rotted: some had moved to
a new domain, some had been rebuilt as client-only apps, and some had simply
shut down. This release repairs what can be repaired and retires what cannot.

## What changed

- **MangaKakalot** — rebuilt for its new home, `mangakakalot.fun`. Search,
  Popular, Latest, details and **full chapter readers** all work again. The
  reader fetches its page list from the site's GraphQL API and decrypts it
  locally (AES-256-GCM), so complete chapters load instead of a 6-image
  preview. Chapter numbers are taken from the site's own badges, so alternate
  scanlation entries no longer show up as bogus chapter numbers.
- **FreeWebNovel** — the site reorganised its URLs; search, popular and latest
  now use the new endpoints and return results again.
- **Removed** three sources that no longer have a working backend:
  - **MangaFire** — its API now requires a single-use, session-bound token
    that cannot be minted outside a browser. No working mirror exists.
  - **LightNovelPub** — every mirror is either Cloudflare-blocked or has shut
    down.
  - **FlameComics** — the domain now redirects to Discord. No working mirror.

## Under the hood

- **Pack covers cleaned up** — dead `bacakomik` hosts and mis-pointed
  `manhwaindo` entries were removed from the bundled packs, and packs were
  regenerated so the affected collections point at live sources again. The pack
  refresher had been reading the wrong field off the search API and silently
  discovering no hosts, which left some collections empty; it now reads the
  aggregated host list and refills every item.
- **Fewer moving parts** — the source pickers, novel-source lists, referers and
  search-relevance rules no longer mention the retired sources.
